title: If already justified, death cannot shut one from heaven—yet Paul bars the unrepentant vicious
source_text: XIX. Praeterea qui jam justificatus est, & cui peccata omnia remissa sunt, hoc ipso idoneus est qui admittatur in regnum coelorum. Et si supponatur in eo statu mori, nihil est propter quod debeat in infernum detrudi, & ab ingressu regni Dei arceri. Nam cui revera sunt omnia peccata remissa, ille est ab omni poena peccati liber, praesertim vero a tormentis inferorum, & gloriae ac felicitatis coelestis privatione. Apostolus autem saepius affirmat, illos qui scelerate vivant, & patrant ea quae carnis opera vocat, non ingressuros in regnum coelorum. Nolite, inquit, errare, neque fornicarii, neque idolis servientes, neque adulteri, neque masculorum concubitores, neque fures, neque avari, neque ebriosi, neque maledici, neque rapaces, regnum Dei possidebunt. 1 Cor. 6. v. 10. Et alibi, postquam varia carnis opera recensuit, subjungit, Quae praedico vobis, sicut praedixi, eos qui talia agunt, regni Dei non fore haeredes. Gal. 5. v. 21. Vel ergo falsum dixit Apostolus, vel falsum est illos, qui scelera jam enumerata designant, necdum illis renunciarunt, jam justificatos esse; aut dicendum, contra sensum communem Christianorum, & manifestam veritatem, peccata quae jam remissa supponuntur, & a quibus aliquis censetur jam justificatus, posse tamen obstare, si mors illum rapiat, quominus in gloriam coelestem admittatur, & etiam efficere, ut aeternis in inferno suppliciis adjudicetur.
pass_a_gloss: Further, whoever is already justified and to whom all sins have been remitted is by that very fact fit to be admitted into the kingdom of heaven. And if he is supposed to die in that state, there is nothing for which he ought to be thrust into hell and barred from entering God's kingdom. For the one to whom all sins are truly remitted is free from every punishment of sin—especially from the torments of hell and from the privation of heavenly glory and happiness. But the Apostle often affirms that those who live wickedly and do what he calls works of the flesh will not enter the kingdom of heaven. Do not be deceived, he says: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who lie with males, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers will possess God's kingdom (1 Cor 6:10). And elsewhere, after listing various works of the flesh, he adds: I warn you, as I warned before, that those who do such things will not be heirs of God's kingdom (Gal 5:21). So either the Apostle spoke falsely, or it is false that those who still mark those listed crimes and have not yet renounced them are already justified; or one must say, against Christians' common sense and clear truth, that sins supposed already remitted—and from which someone is counted already justified—can still, if death snatches him, block entrance to heavenly glory and even cause him to be sentenced to eternal punishments in hell.
pass_b_english: Full remission fits one for heaven if death comes in that state.
Paul bars the unrepentant vicious from the kingdom—so they are not yet justified.

lemmas.gloss: fit for the kingdom of heaven

choices.why: Cannot be true of those still living in listed vices.
